entities.label: Person
entities.summary: Wenceslaus I, Duke of Luxembourg, played a pivotal role in the medieval European power struggle from 1354 until his death in 1383. As the son of John the Blind, King of Bohemia, and Beatrice of Bourbon, he inherited the Duchy of Luxembourg and expanded its borders through strategic alliances and military conquests. His reign was marked by the Luxembourg-Bohemia alliance with the Holy Roman Emperor, Charles IV, and the subsequent conflicts with the Duchy of Burgundy and the Habsburgs. Wenceslaus I's legacy is reflected in the continued relevance of the Luxembourgish crown jewels, which he donated to the Archbishop of Trier, and the establishment of the Duchy of Luxembourg as a major power in the region. He is remembered for his military victories, including the Battle of Waw, which secured his position as Duke of Luxembourg. Wenceslaus I's diplomatic efforts led to the signing of the Treaty of Strasbourg, which recognized Luxembourg's independence and secured its borders. His impact on European politics and diplomacy continues to be felt today.
